public_rationale: IFEval documents substantial instruction-following failures even under its looser scoring rule. The January research report also identifies difficulty detecting reasoning mistakes. These findings support reliability remaining a problem, while the majority of successful IFEval responses rule out interpreting the claim as universal failure.
limitations: Benchmark performance varies by task and scoring method.
This does not establish that every use of an LLM is unreliable or that useful applications require perfect accuracy.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Reliability remains a problem for large language models.

from_speaker: whether the systems reliably deliver what they are asked for
our_interpretation: Reliability means consistently producing correct responses that satisfy explicit requests.
A material, recurring error rate supports this statement; occasional errors alone would not establish that every application is unreliable.

criteria.support_condition: Repeated evaluations of contemporary LLMs show material failures to meet clear instructions or give correct answers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations establish dependable instruction following and correctness across ordinary requests, with reported failures confined to defective tests or exceptional circumstances.
